B10_00: Macrophage chemotaxis toward injury or infection must be damped so inflammatory infiltrates do not persist and cause collateral tissue damage. Negative regulators limit how many macrophages arrive and how far they move, acting through secreted cytokine-like mediators, a complement component whose cleavage products are chemoattractants, a matrix metalloproteinase, a signalling adaptor and a SLAM-family receptor. An estrogen-synthesising enzyme links sex hormone status to inflammation and wound-healing resolution.
B10_01: Granulopoiesis must be braked as well as driven, since unchecked neutrophil and eosinophil production distorts myeloid balance and contributes to leukaemia and inflammatory damage. Transcriptional restraint involves RUNX1, RARA, whose fusion in acute promyelocytic leukaemia arrests promyelocytes, PRDM16 and the dendritic cell factor ZBTB46. INPP5D dampens growth factor phosphoinositide signalling, TRIB1 drives turnover of myeloid transcription factors and CUL4A provides ubiquitin ligase activity, together setting lineage output and emergency granulopoiesis.
B10_02: Negative regulation of mast cell degranulation keeps resting cells quiescent and limits release of histamine and proteases after IgE crosslinking, setting the threshold for allergy and anaphylaxis and preventing bronchoconstriction, vascular leak and itch. Inhibitory immunoreceptors such as CD300A counter activating signals, galectin-9 engages surface receptors, and intracellular RABGEF1 restrains downstream signalling, its absence causing spontaneous skin inflammation in mice. Failure contributes to atopic disease and mast cell hyperreactivity.
B10_03: Brakes on cGAS-STING signalling keep cytosolic DNA-triggered type I interferon and inflammatory responses proportionate, preventing interferonopathies, lupus-like autoimmunity and damaging inflammation. TREX1 degrades cytosolic DNA, cGAS is inhibited by kinase and acyltransferase modifications and by BANF1-mediated chromatin tethering, extracellular cGAMP is hydrolysed, and autophagy factors and adaptors such as SPSB3 limit adaptor lifespan. Phosphatases and DNA-damage proteins PARP1 and PRKDC further connect genome surveillance to reduced interferon output.
B10_04: Antigen-triggered acute inflammation must be actively damped to prevent immune complex injury, anaphylaxis and autoimmunity. The inhibitory Fc gamma receptor FCGR2B raises the activation threshold of B cells, mast cells and phagocytes, and its loss predisposes to systemic autoimmunity. Neuropeptide Y provides a neuroimmune brake, sialophorin (CD43) shapes leukocyte adhesion and contact activation, and others contribute cytokine receptor signalling, together setting hypersensitivity strength and duration.
B10_05: Braking neutrophil migration determines whether inflammation resolves or damages tissue, as in acute lung injury, ischaemia-reperfusion and chronic inflammatory disease. SLIT2 acts through Robo receptors to repel neutrophils and stabilise their cytoskeleton, C5AR2 tempers classical C5a receptor signalling, TNFAIP6 modifies hyaluronan matrix to hinder adhesion and extravasation, and MIR223 restrains myeloid activation. These represent the resolution side of innate immune recruitment.
B10_06: TLR9 senses endosomal unmethylated CpG DNA and drives type I interferon and cytokine production, especially from plasmacytoid dendritic cells, so its signalling must be restrained to avoid autoimmunity such as lupus. A plasmacytoid dendritic cell inhibitory receptor dampens interferon output, a small GTPase limits receptor residence in signalling endosomes, and a receptor phosphatase and lysosomal thioesterase restrain downstream activation, together setting the threshold for DNA sensing and self-tolerance.
B10_07: Restraining leukocyte extravasation keeps inflammation proportionate, preventing neutrophil and monocyte accumulation that damages tissue in sepsis, arthritis and atherosclerosis. Chemokines CXCL12, CCL21, CCL25 and CCL28 pattern cell positioning and can retain cells, prostaglandin E2 acting through EP4 raises cAMP to suppress adhesion, and MIR146A dampens NF-kB output. Phospholipase C beta and a cytokine receptor subunit tune signalling that converts chemotactic cues into firm arrest and diapedesis.
B10_08: Proliferation of immature thymocytes must be curbed so that developmental stages proceed with controlled cell numbers for selection, and loss of these brakes contributes to thymic hyperplasia and lymphoid malignancy. Stromal bone morphogenetic protein and hedgehog ligands limit thymocyte expansion, an INK4A-locus CDK inhibitor enforces arrest, and a transmembrane Wnt regulator tempers proliferative signals. Niche cues and intracellular checkpoints thus balance proliferation and differentiation during T cell development.
B10_09: Restraining osteoclast formation from myeloid precursors preserves bone mass; when it fails, resorption exceeds formation in osteoporosis and inflammatory erosion, while excess restraint gives dense, poorly remodelled bone. Contributors include a claudin whose gastric loss alters systemic signals to bone, a matrix glycoprotein sequestering TGF-beta family ligands, an F-box substrate receptor degrading osteoclastogenic factors, an inhibitory leukocyte receptor dampening ITAM costimulation, and lactoferrin, which favours osteoblasts.
B10_10: Holding myeloid progenitors back from monocyte differentiation preserves proliferating precursors and other lineages; losing the brake shifts output toward monocytes and macrophages, while its persistence blocks maturation as in myeloid leukaemias. CDK6 and MYC keep progenitors cycling rather than maturing, a homeobox factor and the dendritic cell factor ZBTB46 impose alternative programmes, INPP5D dampens growth factor and immune receptor signalling, and a microRNA tunes the decision post-transcriptionally.
B10_11: Brakes on RIG-I sensing of cytoplasmic viral RNA keep interferon production proportionate and self-limiting, preventing sustained output and autoinflammatory damage. LGP2 (DHX58) competes with and modulates duplex RNA recognition, NLRX1 and C1QBP restrain MAVS at the mitochondrial membrane, RNF125 ubiquitinates RIG-I for degradation, and NPLOC4-UFD1 with the p97 segregase feeds components to the proteasome. Loss favours chronic inflammation, and viruses exploit the same nodes.
B10_12: Immunoglobulin production by B cells must be capped, or plasma cell differentiation and class switching cause hypergammaglobulinaemia, autoantibodies and allergic IgE. Inhibitory receptors CD22 and FCGR2B raise activation thresholds, CR1 tunes complement-dependent stimulation, BCL6 holds germinal centre B cells undifferentiated, FOXP3 marks regulatory T cells suppressing helper signals, and NDFIP1 promotes ubiquitin-mediated limitation; IL-33 and decoy IL-13 receptor components link tissue signals to restraint of type 2 responses.
B10_13: Granulocyte chemotaxis must be braked so neutrophil and eosinophil influx resolves rather than destroying tissue, since failure favours persistent neutrophilic inflammation in sepsis, arthritis and chronic lung disease. Mechanisms include a decoy-like anaphylatoxin receptor tempering C5a receptor signalling, a surface peptidase trimming chemokines and neuropeptides, a secreted axon guidance cue repelling leukocytes, a hyaluronan-binding protein limiting transmigration, and a myeloid microRNA restraining differentiation and activation.
B10_14: Restraining B lineage commitment and maturation prevents marrow output skewing toward lymphoid cells and enlarges less the pool needing screening for self-reactivity. ID2 sequesters E-proteins such as E2A that would activate the B cell programme, activin and inhibin subunits supply TGF-beta family signals suppressing lymphoid differentiation, SFRP1 dampens Wnt signalling in the niche, and HMGB3 keeps progenitors uncommitted, while complement receptor CR1 links immune complex feedback to B cells.
B10_15: Negative regulation of macrophage cytokine production keeps inflammation proportionate and allows resolution; its loss underlies septic shock, chronic inflammation and fibrosis, while excess leaves macrophages tolerant. Intracellularly IRAK3 acts as a catalytically inactive decoy kinase blocking NF-kB activation downstream of Toll-like receptors and CUEDC2 dampens inflammatory transcription; extracellularly the three TGF-beta ligands act in autocrine and paracrine fashion to suppress pro-inflammatory genes and promote a reparative state.
B10_16: Damping cellular responses to interferon-gamma limits classical macrophage polarisation and preserves repair phenotypes; failure contributes to autoimmunity, whereas excess braking aids tumour immune evasion and poor pathogen control. A phosphatase dephosphorylates JAK kinases and STAT1 to end signalling, liver X receptors and PPARG transcriptionally oppose interferon-induced programmes, a macrodomain ADP-ribosyltransferase biases signalling toward STAT6, and arginase 1 consumes arginine otherwise used by inducible nitric oxide synthase.
B10_17: Brakes on NLRP3 inflammasome assembly prevent caspase-1 activation, IL-1beta and IL-18 release and pyroptosis from tipping into chronic inflammation; their loss underlies periodic fever syndromes and contributes to gout, atherosclerosis and neuroinflammation. TRIM31 and FBXL2 ubiquitinate NLRP3 for degradation, IRGM and LAMP2-dependent autophagy clear it, PYDC1 and PYDC2 act as pyrin-domain decoys, and depalmitoylases, kinases and SIRT2 tune it; other NLRs and TREM2 add inhibitory input.
B10_18: Restraining regulatory T cell differentiation limits accumulated suppression, favouring effector expansion against pathogens and tumours, while excessive restraint risks autoimmunity. TNFSF4 (OX40 ligand) signals to conventional T cells and opposes the induced Treg programme, CTLA4, LAG3 and IRF1 shape the environment in which FOXP3 is induced, midkine skews differentiation away from the regulatory fate, and microRNAs such as miR-21 tune it; proteasome subunits degrade lineage factors and affect antigen presentation.
B10_19: Braking T cell migration retains activated cells in lymph nodes, limits infiltration of inflamed or immunoprivileged tissue and prevents autoimmune damage, though tumours exploit it to exclude effector cells. CD69, an early activation marker, blocks egress from lymphoid tissue, CD200 engaging CD200R1 delivers inhibitory signals to myeloid and lymphoid cells, and RIPOR2 and LRCH1 act on Rho-family GTPase signalling to dampen chemokine-driven adhesion and polarisation.
B10_20: Th1 responses providing interferon-gamma-dependent defence must be restrained to avoid tissue damage and autoimmunity. IL-27, formed from EBI3 and signalling through IL27RA with IL6ST, limits Th1 and Th17 differentiation and promotes regulatory programmes; HAVCR2 (TIM-3) engaged by galectin-9 drives exhaustion or death of interferon-gamma-producing effectors; a soluble binding protein sequesters IL-18; and IL-33 via IL1RL1 skews toward type 2 immunity. Excess restraint in tumours blunts antitumour activity.
B10_21: Type I interferon signalling must be shut off once infection clears, since sustained output damages tissue and causes autoinflammatory disease. TREX1 and SAMHD1 prevent self nucleic acids triggering chronic interferon, as loss causes Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome, and ADAR editing marks endogenous double-stranded RNA as self. USP18 removes ISG15 conjugates and blocks JAK-STAT at the receptor, PTPN2 dephosphorylates components, and METTL3/YTHDF m6A decay, CNOT7 deadenylation and EIF4E2-GIGYF2 translational repression limit interferon transcripts.
B10_22: Restraining dendritic cell differentiation from myeloid progenitors limits T cell priming capacity and favours tolerance to self, transplanted and fetal tissue, while losing restraint contributes to autoimmunity. ITIM-bearing inhibitory receptors FCGR2B, CLEC12A and LILRB1 recruit phosphatases dampening activating signals, and HLA-G is a non-classical ligand mediating immune privilege. TMEM176A and TMEM176B act intracellularly to maintain immaturity, and ZBTB46 marks classical dendritic cells while limiting their activation.
B10_23: Holding back macrophage differentiation keeps progenitors available or directs them to other fates, and too little restraint expands inflammatory macrophages, contributing to atherosclerotic plaque growth and adipose inflammation. GATA2 sustains earlier progenitor programmes and ZBTB46 enforces the conventional dendritic cell alternative; secreted inhibin and activin subunits and adipocyte-derived adiponectin act from outside; and the RNA-binding protein QKI and the phosphatase PTPN2 limit cytokine receptor signalling driving maturation.
B10_24: Negative regulation of monocyte chemotaxis damps recruitment from blood toward chemokine gradients, limiting prolonged inflammatory damage and shaping atherosclerotic lesions, fibrotic scars and wound healing through the number of monocyte-derived macrophages arriving. Secreted CCN3, NBL1 and GREM1 act extracellularly, SLIT2 signals through Robo receptors to block directed myeloid migration, DUSP1 dephosphorylates MAP kinases to curtail inflammatory signalling, and SLAMF8 tempers macrophage responses.
